label: fs-the-intersection-of-the-empty-family-is-the-empty-set
tail:
VERDICT: CLEAN

BOUNDARY:
- empty set ∅: L1 correctly states no elements; step 2.1 correctly uses this to get vacuous truth of the condition.
- empty family ∅: the case under refutation; steps 2.1–3.1 correctly show the condition would give a set containing all sets, contradicting L3/L4.
- ∅ as an element of the hypothetical c: step 2.1 includes ∅; step 4.1 correctly shows that c = ∅ would then give ∅ ∈ ∅, impossible by L1.
- universal quantifier over the empty set: vacuous truth properly applied in step 2.1.
- both directions of the defining biconditional: the forward direction (condition ⇒ membership) is the only one needed in step 2.1, and it is justified.
- domain includes ∅: L1 guarantees ∅ is a set, so it is available for quantification.

CHECKED: Verified every numbered step (1.1–4.1) and every cited fact (L1–L4) against the full reproduced text of all dependencies; each citation is faithful and the reasoning is mathematically licensed.
